G2.2 and G2.3 do not flag that `engines/hermes/modules/sa_plan/sa_plan_store.ml` (`M`), `test/dune` (`M`), and `test/test_sa_plan_job_budget.ml` (`D`) are M1 (`2ab40165`, authored after A2), risking reverting M1's retry-budget fix during G2 hunk integration.

G3.3 invokes bare `jj resolve` (which launches an interactive TUI merge tool that hangs or fails in non-interactive `bash -c`) and §16.2 sets a global Andon stop on 'A conflict resolution that would drop lines' (which blocks any 3-way code conflict resolution that replaces superseded lines).

G6.3 runs `tools/sa-plan job enqueue` onto `uos-agy-review-20261025` without invoking a dispatcher (`agy_dispatch_cli`) or using a write-capable queue, and G6.2/G6.3 omit `roots(...)` when selecting `<first own commit>` for `jj rebase -s`.

findings.issue: G0.5 creates `preserved/div-<change12>-<commit12>` on all 14 sides of the 7 divergent changes, keeping all 14 commits visible, while G0.10 states that abandoning the losing side can wait ('G0 doesn't wait for this. The §7 VCS row checks `::<tip>` only'). In `jj 0.44`, `divergent()` matches every visible commit whose `change_id` is shared by another visible commit. Consequently: (1) if one side of any divergent change is already in `::main` (`2ab40165`), `::main & divergent()` is non-empty and fails G1.5's §7 VCS row (`jj log -r '::<tip> & (conflicts() | divergent())'`); (2) when G5.2 merges `rnqmowpo`, `lwmwqpun`, or `yzmpqqrk` via two-parent merge (`jj new main <h>` / `jj new @ <h>`), `<h>` enters `::<tip>` while its sibling remains visible under `preserved/div-*`, failing §7's VCS row; (3) if Codex instead runs `jj abandon <loser>` (G0.10), `jj` moves the `preserved/div-*` bookmark off `<loser>` onto `<loser>-`; and (4) three of the 7 divergent changes in §3 (`qnppzponnttw`, `zosuwowvmzst`, `owuunmmlvuts`) are not accounted for in any generation's ledger.
findings.recommendation: To preserve the losing side under `preserved/div-*` while clearing `divergent()`, have the owner (Codex) run `jj duplicate <loser_commit_id>` (creating an identical snapshot commit with a fresh `change_id`), point `preserved/div-<change12>-<commit12>` at the duplicated commit, and then run `jj abandon <loser_commit_id>` before G1.5 (or integrate EV-01 fixes in G5.2 via `jj restore --from <chosen_commit_id>` into a fresh commit in `$M`). Explicitly account for `qnppzponnttw`, `zosuwowvmzst`, and `owuunmmlvuts` in the G1/G5 ledgers.

findings.issue: G5.2 and G5.3 instruct Codex to merge EV-01 fixes and `D1..D10` using the chaining method (`first jj new main <h>, then jj new @ <h>`), running `km-gate --gate` after each, and state: 'A head that isn't fit on its first attempt is seed-banked immediately (P3 override, §5.3).' Once `jj new @ <D_k>` runs, `@` IS the merge commit containing `D_k`. If `D_k` fails `km-gate --gate` or conflicts, G5.3 gives no command to back `@` off to `@-`: running `jj new @ <D_{k+1}>` for the next head chains `D_{k+1}` on top of the unfit merge commit (retaining `D_k` in `::@` and `main`), whereas applying §4.3 rule 3 (`jj new main`) discards all previously chained fit heads in G5.
findings.recommendation: Specify in §6 preamble and G5.2–G5.3 that when a chained head `<h>` is unfit on its merge into `@`, Codex bookmarks `<h>` under `preserved/failed-g5-<commit12>` and backs `@` off to the previous fit commit in the chain (`jj abandon @ && jj edit <last_fit_commit>`) before chaining the next head with `jj new @ <next_head>`.

findings.issue: §6 preamble (lines 368–373) orders every generation that moves `main` as: `2. Write the generation journal and ledger into $M ... and commit them in the candidate. 3. Run §7, including the Docs rows on that journal. 4. Lease and move main.` At the same time, §6 line 366 and §7 lines 484–486 require recording §7's exact commands, exit codes, counts, durations, and output digests in the generation journal and bind §7 to the exact candidate tip commit ID. A journal written and committed in Step 2 (before §7 runs) cannot contain §7's results; editing the journal in `$M` after Step 3 to record §7's outputs mutates the candidate commit (changing its `commit_id`), invalidating §7's commit-ID binding and leaving the updated journal unchecked by `journal-check`, `diagram-check`, and `timestamp-check`.
findings.recommendation: Split Steps 2–3 in §6 preamble: (2a) run all §7 build/test/formal/telegram/provenance/risk rows on the candidate code tree in `$M`; (2b) write the complete generation journal and ledger (recording those rows' exit codes, counts, durations, and output digests) into `$M`; and (3) run the non-mutating §7 `Docs` (`timestamp-check`, `diagram-check`, `journal-check`), `Secrets`, `VCS`, `Accounting`, and `Damping` rows on the resulting final commit ID with no further edits before Step 4 (lease and move `main`).

findings.issue: In G7, step 4 ('Refresh the off-host copies (G0.8–0.9 screen and push); score the forecasts (§15)') runs BEFORE step 5 ('Final programme journal: commit it into `$M` on top of `main` -> Docs rows -> leased journal-only move of `main`'). Advancing `main` in G7.5 after G7.4's off-host push leaves the final `main` tip unpushed to GitHub `origin` and unbacked-up on `vm-1`, violating §10 L7 ('Off-host copy in G0 and refreshed at every move') and G0.9's pass condition (`main@origin == main`). Additionally, §5.4 line 327 (`G7 main after: unchanged`) and §6 line 376 ('Generations that don't move `main` (G0, G1, G7)') contradict G7.5's leased move of `main`.
findings.recommendation: Swap G7.4 and G7.5 so the final programme journal is committed in `$M`, verified by §7, and landed on `main` under lease BEFORE scoring forecasts and running the final G0.8–0.9 off-host push and `vm-1` backup refresh, and update §5.4's G7 `main after` column to `G7 journal tip`.

findings.issue:
In `20261025-0738-merge-plan-deferred-trunk-code.txt` (lines 4–32), the 29 `agent-surface` paths are `.agents/*` (7), `.claude/*` (7), `.codex/*` (7), `.gemini/*` (7), and `GEMINI.md` (line 32), not root `AGENTS.md`. || test -e

` in G1.5b and G2.5 will fail on broken symlink targets unless those 4 `SKILL.md` files are integrated before G2.5 checks them.

findings.issue: G0.5 creates `preserved/div-suukkrkqkwuv-<commit12>` before G0.6 quiesces writers and without running `jj -R $U status` to ensure `$U`'s 998 working-copy files on disk are snapshotted into `default@`. If any file on disk in `$U` was modified after `suukkrkqkwuv`'s last snapshot, G4.2 (`jj restore --from preserved/div-suukkrkqkwuv-<side>`) will miss it, and G4.8 (`verify jj -R $U status ...; run jj -R $U new main`) will snapshot those changes into a new unbookmarked commit on `suukkrkqkwuv` and immediately orphan it when `jj -R $U new main` runs. Moreover, G4.2 neither gives the command to identify which side of `suukkrkqkwuv` (`892008ae2734` vs `c29b1127cd9f`) is `default@` nor reconciles the non-`default@` side (`feat(telegram): Slice 2 supervised OTP actor API`) before G0.10 abandons the loser.
findings.recommendation: In G0.5 (after quiescing writers), run `jj -R $U status` once so `$U` on disk is snapshotted into `default@` before bookmarking `preserved/div-suukkrkqkwuv-*` and creating `$BK/jj.tar`, and record `DEFAULT_SIDE=$(jj -R $U --ignore-working-copy log -r @ --no-graph -T 'commit_id.short(12)')`. In G4.2, also diff `892008ae2734` against `c29b1127cd9f` so no Slice 2 work on the other side is lost, and pass `--ignore-working-copy` in G4.8 before `jj -R $U new main`.

findings.issue: G3.3 instructs Codex: `After each merge: jj resolve without dropping either side's lines, then focused tests`, and §16.2 sets a global Andon stop on `A conflict resolution that would drop lines`. In `jj 0.44`, bare `jj resolve` launches an interactive TUI merge tool (`:builtin`) that hangs or fails in non-interactive `bash -c` subshells. Furthermore, resolving a 3-way conflict in code (`*.gleam`, `*.ml`, `*.lean`) where a newer implementation replaces an older expression (such as C3's Oct 11 numeric repair vs G2's `Telegram_Numeric_Contract.lean`) necessarily drops superseded lines; applying §16.2 globally to code merges triggers an unconditional Andon stop on any code conflict.
findings.recommendation: Replace bare `jj resolve` in G3.3 with `jj resolve --list` and non-interactive file edits in `$M` (verifying `jj log -r '@ & conflicts()'` is empty), check in G3.2 whether C1, C2, or C3 is already superseded in `main` after G2, and scope the 'without dropping either side's lines' constraint in G3.3 and §16.2 to additive ledgers/evidence while requiring code conflicts to preserve behavior verified by tests and R5 review.

findings.issue: G0.8 runs `jj diff --from root() --to <rev> --name-only` for the secret screen, which inspects only the tip snapshot of `<rev>` and misses any secret, credential, or `.sqlite3` file committed in an intermediate ancestor of `main@origin..<rev>` and deleted before `<rev>`. Additionally, G0.9(a) pushes `-b main -b 'glob:recovery/*' -b 'glob:preserved/trunk-*' -b 'glob:preserved/div-*'` in a single `jj git push` command; if any `preserved/div-*` commit contains a conflict (which `jj 0.44` refuses without `--allow-conflicts`) or if `preserved/trunk-a2-20261025` / `preserved/div-suukkrkqkwuv-*` (containing `validate.exe` and the un-triaged 998-file `W` tree) triggers a hold, the entire command aborts and leaves `main` and `recovery/*` unpushed to `origin`.
findings.recommendation: In G0.8, scan modified paths across all commits in `main@origin..<rev>` (e.g., `jj log -r 'main@origin..<rev>' --summary`) and include `*.exe` in the screen. In G0.9(a), push `-b main -b 'glob:recovery/*'` in a separate first `jj git push` command before pushing `preserved/trunk-*` and `preserved/div-*` (passing `--allow-conflicts` only on `preserved/div-*` if required).

findings.issue: In G6.3, `tools/sa-plan job enqueue <id> <name> uos-agy-review-20261025 <agy-worker> ...` only inserts a row into `var/sa-plan/uos.sqlite3` without invoking an AGY dispatcher (`agy_dispatch_cli`), targets a read-only review queue (`uos-agy-review-20261025`) for a write operation (`jj rebase` in `agy-telemetry-20261024`), and passes `"source":"vuystwzk"` (B2's tip) instead of B2's root own commit. Likewise, G6.2's `jj log -r 'main..ptslsmlx ~ ::preserved/trunk-a2-20261025'` returns all own commits of B1 rather than the first (root-most) own commit required by `jj rebase -s`.
findings.recommendation: In G6.2 and G6.3, select the first own commit with `roots(main..<head> ~ ::preserved/trunk-a2-20261025)`, and in G6.3 specify the dispatcher invocation (`agy_dispatch_cli` or `job claim` + AGY workspace execution + `job complete`) on a write-enabled queue for `agy-telemetry-20261024`.

findings.issue: §5.4 (line 321) and §6 preamble (line 376) classify G1 as a generation that does not move `main` and carries its journal into G2 (G1.9). However, G1.5a, G1.5b, and G1.6 instruct Codex to make a 'leased repair commit on `main` in G1' if landed `ev98_*` files, skill symlinks, or A'/M1 regressions require fixing in G1. Moving `main` in G1 while deferring the G0/G1 journals to G2 violates the §6 preamble (`journal -> §7 -> move`) and §10 L7 (off-host refresh at every move).
findings.recommendation: Specify in G1.5a–G1.6 that if G1 makes a leased repair commit on `main`, it must follow the full §6 generation order (commit the G0/G1 journals and G1.1 lineage note into the repair candidate in `$M` -> run §7 -> lease and move `main` -> refresh off-host copy -> regenerate the G2 companion ledger against the new `main`).

findings.issue: G7.1 compares `jj -R <ws> --ignore-working-copy file list > tracked.txt` (which outputs paths relative to `<ws>`, e.g., `apps/...`) against `find <ws> -type f ...` (which outputs paths prefixed with `<ws>/`, e.g., `/home/an/.../.uos-workspaces/<ws>/apps/...`), and writes `tracked.txt` without specifying a temp path outside `<ws>`. Because the path prefixes differ, comparing the two lists matches 0 files and archives all tracked files in `<ws>` as untracked.
findings.recommendation: Run the comparison from inside `<ws>` with normalized relative paths: `(cd <ws> && comm -23 <(find . -type f -not -path './.jj/*' -not -path './build/*' -not -path './_build/*' -not -path './target/*' -not -path './node_modules/*' | sed 's|^\./||' | sort) <(jj --ignore-working-copy file list | sort))`.

findings.issue: §7's `Damping` row (`repair lines ÷ generation lines ≤ 3%`) and §16.2 (`Damping > 3%` Andon stop) have no minimum line floor. In small generations such as G3 (C1/C2/C3), G5 (EV-01 fixes), G6 (B1/B2 grafts), or a G1 repair commit, total changed lines may be < 100, so even a 3-line merge adjustment exceeds 3% and forces an Andon stop. Additionally, §7's `Docs` row (`bash tools/diagram-check <new docs>`) does not distinguish newly authored merge journals from the 70+ historical evidence `.md` files integrated in G2.6/G4.4/G5.3.
findings.recommendation: Define the §7 `Damping` threshold with a small-generation floor (`repair lines ≤ max(3% of generation lines, 25 lines)`), and scope `diagram-check <new docs>` in §7 to docs newly authored in the merge generation while reporting pre-existing debt on historical evidence docs without editing them.

findings.issue: G2.2 instructs Codex to first restore the 48 `A` code paths in module groups and run `gleam build` and focused tests per group, and then surgically edit `M` paths tagged `trunk-newer`. Because many of the 48 `A` files in `apps/cepaf_gleam` (e.g., `telegram_*_test.gleam`, `restoration_observer*.gleam`, `agy_dispatch*.gleam`) depend on functions and types defined in the 68 `M` files (`gateway/telegram.gleam`, `mcp/tools.gleam`, `web/server.gleam`, `cepaf_gleam.gleam`), running `gleam build` on `A` files before integrating their corresponding `M` hunks will fail compilation.
findings.recommendation: In G2.2, group related `A` files and `trunk-newer` `M` hunks together by module/feature slice before running `gleam build` and focused tests on each group.
